description: Attio is a CRM with a public REST API and a hosted MCP server for AI tools to access and manage workspace CRM data.
access_model: Self-serve: Attio offers a Free plan for up to 3 users, a 14-day Pro trial for new workspaces, and paid Plus, Pro, and Ultra plans; the REST API is accessed with a workspace API key or OAuth app token, while the hosted MCP is available on every plan.
api_breadth: Broad JSON-over-HTTPS REST surface under the v2 API, with documented read/write endpoints for standard objects such as people, companies, users, deals, and workspaces, plus lists, activities, webhooks, OAuth, and SCIM; requests are rate-limited to 100 reads/s and 25 writes/s across the API.
mcp_status: Available: Attio documents a hosted MCP server at https://mcp.attio.com/mcp. It supports OAuth, workspace-scoped CRM read/write tools (records, activities, lists, views, comments, notes, tasks, meetings/calls, emails, workspace, reporting), and a read-only SQL tool that is not available on every billing plan.
blockers: API calls require an access token and endpoint-specific scopes.
Workspace-level OAuth tokens can only be granted by workspace admins; user-level OAuth tokens are limited by the approving member's permissions and require PKCE.
The API is rate-limited to 100 read requests per second and 25 write requests per second, with possible lower limits for specific high-volume endpoints.
Unpublished OAuth apps can be installed in up to 25 workspaces until shared or published.
The MCP SQL query tool is not available on every billing plan.

description: Twenty is an open-source CRM with workspace-generated APIs for CRM records and metadata, plus an official MCP server for AI clients.
auth_methods: API key via Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
access_model: Self-serve: Twenty Cloud offers a free trial without a credit card and paid Pro/Organization plans; self-hosting is available at no cost on the Free (Self-Hosted) plan. API keys are created in workspace Settings, while OAuth clients use dynamic registration.
api_breadth: Workspace-specific Core and Metadata APIs over REST and GraphQL. Core API supports CRUD/querying for people, companies, opportunities, and custom objects; Metadata API manages objects, fields, and relations. GraphQL additionally supports batch upserts and relation traversal. Documented limits are 100 requests/minute and batches of up to 60 records.
mcp_status: Official native MCP server confirmed. Cloud and self-hosted workspaces expose /mcp; it supports OAuth (recommended) or API-key authentication and exposes record, discovery, metadata, workflow, dashboard, view, role, agent, email, calendar, file, and other built-in tools subject to the authenticated user's/API key role permissions.
blockers: An API key must be created in a Twenty workspace under Settings → Developers → API, or an OAuth client must be registered dynamically.
The API is workspace-schema-specific and its workspace-specific API documentation becomes available after creating an API key.
Documented API rate limit is 100 requests per minute; batch operations are limited to 60 records per request.
Cloud access is trial/paid after the trial; the no-cost access path documented by Twenty is self-hosting.

evidence.claim: Twenty exposes workspace-specific REST and GraphQL endpoints generated from each workspace schema.
evidence.excerpt: There is no static API reference for Twenty. Each workspace has its own schema — when you add a custom object (say `Invoice`), it immediately gets REST and GraphQL endpoints identical to built-in objects like `Company` or `Person`. The API is generated from the schema, so endpoints use your object and field names directly — no opaque IDs. Your workspace-specific API documentation is available under Settings → Developers → API after creating an API key. It includes an interactive playground where you can execute real calls against your data. Core API — `/rest/` and `/graphql/` CRUD on records: People, Companies, Opportunities, your custom objects. Query, filter, traverse relations. Metadata API — `/rest/metadata/` and `/metadata/` Schema management: create/modify/delete objects, fields, and relations. Both are available as REST and GraphQL. GraphQL adds batch upserts and the ability to traverse relations in a single query.
